name: Adi Jagannatha Perumal Temple
deity: Adi Jagannatha Perumal (Vishnu), with Padmasini Thayar
significance: One of the 108 Divya Desams glorified in the Naalayira Divya Prabandham, standing near the Sethu coast in Ramanathapuram district. Believed to date to the late 8th century, it was enlarged over the centuries by Chola, Pandya, Nayak and Sethupathi rulers.
story: Rama is said to have lain on darbha grass here, performing penance to compel the ocean to yield him a path to Lanka.

name: Sathyamurthi Perumal Temple
significance: A 9th-century Pallava rock-cut shrine counted among the 108 Divya Desams, today protected by the Archaeological Survey of India. It houses one of the largest reclining (Anantasayana) Vishnu images in India.
story: The Brahmanda Purana tells that the sage Satya won a boon here that Vishnu would appear whenever wished, and a king was directed to raise the temple.

name: Shri Naimishnath Vishnu Temple
deity: Devaraja Perumal (Naimishnath Vishnu), with Pundarikavalli Thayar
significance: The Vishnu temple of the sacred Naimisha forest on the Gomti, one of the 108 Divya Desams and counted among the eight self-manifested (Swayamvyakta) Vishnu shrines. The surrounding forest is revered as the place where the Puranas were first recited to the assembled sages.
story: Indra is said to have performed penance to Vishnu at Naimisha for two thousand years to overcome the asura Vritra.

name: Narsingh Temple, Joshimath
builtDisplay: trad. founded by Adi Shankara (8th c.)
significance: The main temple of Joshimath, seat of the uttaramnaya matha founded by Adi Shankara, whose Narasimha idol is traditionally held to have been installed by the acharya himself. It is revered among the 108 Vishnu shrines sung by the Tamil Alvar saints.
story: The idol's left wrist grows ever thinner; when it finally breaks, the Nar and Narayan mountains are to merge and Badrinath will reappear as a black stone at Bhavishya Badri.

name: Raghunath Temple, Devprayag
significance: A Rama temple of the 108 Divya Desams standing above the confluence where the Alaknanda and Bhagirathi unite to form the Ganga. Traditionally established by Adi Shankara, with evidence of existence by the 9th-10th century and later Garhwal royal expansion.
story: Rama is believed to have done penance here to cleanse himself of the sin of slaying Ravana, a Brahmin king.

name: Navamohana Krishna Temple
significance: The Divya Desam of Thiruvaipadi (Aypadi) at Gokul on the Yamuna, regarded as the scene of Krishna's childhood among the cowherds and sung by several Alvars including Andal. The present small shrine is a modern replacement for an older temple lost to political upheavals.
story: Here Krishna is said to have danced upon the subdued serpent Kaliya in the Yamuna before the people of Gokul.

name: Ahobilam Narasimha Temples
significance: A pilgrimage complex of nine Narasimha shrines spread over Upper and Lower Ahobilam in the Nallamala hills, revered as a canonical Divya Desam sung in the Periya Tirumoli. Its temples took their present form under Vijayanagara patronage, notably of the Saluva and Tuluva dynasties including Krishnadevaraya.

name: Tiruvetkalam Pasupatheswarar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam revered in Sambandar's Tevaram hymns, today standing within the Annamalai University campus near Chidambaram. The Chola-built complex was renovated in 1914 by a Chettiar patron.
story: Arjuna is said to have won the Pasupatha weapon here after Shiva tested him in the guise of a hunter.

name: Sivapuri Uchinathar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam of the Tevaram canon, counted third in the series of shrines on the northern bank of the Kaveri. The temple fell into disrepair and was rebuilt in the early twentieth century.
story: The boy-saint Sambandar, travelling to his own wedding, is said to have been miraculously fed here and praised Shiva as Uchinathar.

name: Tirukkazhippalai Palvannanathar Temple
significance: A Shiva shrine of the Paadal Petra Sthalam canon near Chidambaram, revered in the 7th-century Tevaram hymns of the Nayanmars. Its lord bears the name 'the milk-hued one'.
story: A king's horse is said to have split the lingam with its hoof, and the wound was healed by milk poured by the celestial cow Kamadhenu.

name: Achalpuram Shivalokathyagar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam glorified in the Tevaram, held sacred as the place where the child-saint Sambandar ended his earthly life. Tradition places his wedding here, after which he and the assembly merged into the divine light.
story: Saint Sambandar's spirit is believed to have merged with Shiva at this shrine on his wedding day.

name: Mahendrapalli Tirumeni Azhagar Temple
significance: One of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, its 'beautiful-bodied lord' praised by Tirugnanasambandar in the Tevaram. The shrine stands near the Kollidam in Mayiladuthurai district.
story: Mahendra is believed to have worshipped Shiva here, giving the village its name.

name: Mullaivananathar Temple
deity: Mullaivana Nathar (Shiva), with Ani Konda Kothai Ammai
significance: A coastal Paadal Petra Sthalam on the northern bank of the Kaveri delta, glorified by Tirugnanasambandar in the Tevaram. Its construction is traditionally credited to the Early Chola king Killivalavan.
story: The goddess of the shrine is herself said to have received her initiation at this place.

name: Sayavaneswarar Temple
significance: A Shiva shrine of the Tevaram canon beside the ancient port of Kaveripoompattinam, dating from the Medieval Chola period. It is counted among the six temples held equal in sanctity to Kasi.

name: Pallavaneswarar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam at the archaeological site of Poompuhar, the drowned Sangam-era port city, and the birthplace of the saint-poet Pattinathar. It is glorified in the Tevaram hymns of Tirugnanasambandar.
story: A Pallava king is believed to have attained salvation at this shrine.

name: Swetharanyeswarar Temple
significance: The 'white forest' shrine, a Paadal Petra Sthalam and one of the nine Navagraha temples, dedicated to Budha (Mercury). Founded under the Cholas, whose inscriptions survive alongside Pandya and Vijayanagara records, its present masonry is 16th-century Vijayanagara work.
story: Shiva is said to have taken the fierce form of Aghoramurthi beneath a tree here to destroy the demon Maruthuvasuran.

name: Velladainatha Swami Temple
deity: Velladainatha Swami (Shiva as Somaskanda), with Kaviaganni
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam where Shiva is worshipped in the Somaskanda form, with attendant shrines of Ganesha, Durga and Murugan. Its glory was sung by the Saivite saints in the medieval Tevaram poems.
story: The saint Sundarar is believed to have been cleansed of sin at Thirukkurukavur after his victory in debate over the Jains.

name: Sattainathar Temple, Sirkazhi
deity: Sattainathar / Brahmapureeswarar (Shiva in three forms), with Thirunilainayaki
significance: A vast three-tiered Paadal Petra Sthalam where Shiva is worshipped on three levels as Brahmapureeswarar, Toniappar and the Bhairava form Sattainathar. The shrine of the Nayanmar age was greatly enlarged by the later Cholas from Kulothunga I to Kulothunga III, and is the storied birthplace of the saint Sambandar's devotion.
story: When the infant Sambandar cried at the temple tank, Parvati herself nursed him, and he burst forth with the first hymn of the Tevaram.

name: Vaitheeswaran Koil
deity: Vaidyanathar (Shiva, the divine healer), with Thaiyalnayagi
significance: The temple of Shiva as the 'god of healing', a Paadal Petra Sthalam and one of the nine Navagraha temples, associated with Mars (Angaraka). Inscriptions run from Kulothunga Chola I, with later endowments by Pandya, Nayak and Maratha rulers.
story: The planet-god Angaraka, stricken with leprosy, is said to have been cured here by Vaidyanatha, and so the shrine became his Navagraha seat.

name: Sivalokanathar Temple, Tirupunkur
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam a few miles west of Vaitheeswaran Koil, remembered above all for the Dalit saint Nandanar, one of the 63 Nayanmars. The shrine stands in Tamil tradition as an emblem of devotion crossing caste barriers.
story: At Shiva's command the Nandi before the sanctum moved aside so that Nandanar, barred at the gate, could behold the lord.

name: Thiruneedur Somanathaswami Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam on the Kaveri's northern bank, its lord praised in the Tevaram by Tirunavukkarasar and Sundarar. The temple is documented among the Later Chola foundations of the Kulottunga I to Rajendra III era.
story: A demon reborn as a crab for his sins is said to have sought liberation here on the sage Narada's counsel.

name: Kalyanasundareswarar Temple, Thiruvelvikudi
significance: A Kaveri-bank Paadal Petra Sthalam venerated in the Tevaram hymns of Sambandar and Sundarar. Tradition associates the shrine with the Ardhanarisvara form, in which Shiva shared half his body with Parvati.
story: The saint Sundarar is said to have bathed in the Agni theertham here to be cured of his illness.

name: Tirumanancheri Udhvaganathar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam on the Kaveri, sung by Sambandar and Tirunavukkarasar, and famed across Tamil Nadu as the 'wedding place' of Shiva. Devotees seeking marriage flock to its Kalyanasundareswarar shrine.

name: Korukkai Veeratteswarar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam and one of the eight Ashta Veeratta shrines commemorating Shiva's deeds of valour, here the subduing of Kama, the god of desire. The 9th-century Chola structure was later expanded by the Thanjavur Nayaks.
story: The sage Theerthapahu, whose hands withered for slighting the temple's sacred water, is said to have been made whole by Shiva after penance.

name: Karuppariyalur Kutram Poruttha Naathar Temple
deity: Kutram Poruttha Naathar (Shiva who forgives faults), with Kolvalai Naayaki
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam whose lord bears the name 'he who bears with transgressions' (Aparadhakshameswarar). The shrine was hymned by Tirugnanasambandar and Sundarar in the Tevaram.

name: Keezhaiyur Kadaimudinathar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam on the northern bank of the Kaveri near Poompuhar, glorified by Tirugnanasambandar in the Tevaram poems.
story: Brahma himself is believed to have worshipped Shiva at this shrine.

name: Mela Kadambur Amirthakadeswarar Temple
significance: A rare karakkoil — a temple sculpted as a festival chariot, its vimana shaped like a wheeled car — built under emperor Kulottunga Chola I. It is the 88th Paadal Petra Sthalam, sung by Tirunavukkarasar and Sundarar.
story: Indra is said to have sought to carry the shrine to heaven, but Ganesha pinned its chariot wheel to the earth so the lord would remain for worship here.

name: Kanattampuliyur Pathanchalinathar Temple
deity: Pathanchalinathar / Patanjaleeswarar (Shiva), with Kola Valai Kai Ambicai
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam of the Nava Puliyur group of nine 'tiger-town' shrines, glorified by Sundarar in the Tevaram. It is held to be a dwelling place of the sage Patanjali.
story: The sages Patanjali and Vyaghrapada are believed to have worshipped Shiva at this Puliyur.

name: Sakshinatheswarar Temple, Thiruppurambiyam
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam at the site of the 9th-century Battle of Thirupurambiyam, whose outcome opened the way for the Chola resurgence under Aditya I, builder of an early shrine here. The present masonry structure is 16th-century Nayak work, and the site ranks among the noted centres of Dakshinamurthy worship.
story: Shiva is said to have descended as a witness for a Chettiar lady in a dispute, earning the name Sakshinathar, 'the lord who bore witness'.

name: Vijayamangai Vijayanatheswarar Temple
significance: A Medieval Chola temple of the 'lord of victory', counted among the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams and hymned by Tirugnanasambandar and Tirunavukkarasar.
story: Shiva is said to have granted Arjuna the Pasupata weapon here after both shot the demon Mookasura during Arjuna's penance.

name: Thiruvisanallur Sivayoginathar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam on the Kaveri's northern bank whose oldest masonry was raised in the reign of Parantaka I, with 16th-century Thanjavur Nayak expansions. Its early Chola sculpture, including powerfully carved vyalas, is noted by art historians.
story: A king of Kerala is said to have worshipped here to be freed of a curse incurred by mistreating women.

name: Kodeeswarar Temple, Kottaiyur
significance: A granite Paadal Petra Sthalam on the western outskirts of Kumbakonam, revered in the 7th-century Tevaram. The temple takes part in the Mahamaham festival held in Kumbakonam every twelve years.
story: Suruchi, cursed into a demon's form, is said to have regained his own after bathing in the temple's sacred spring.

name: Innambur Ezhutharinathar Temple
significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam near Kumbakonam whose sanctum carries a rare Gajaprashta (elephant-back) vimana over a self-manifested lingam. The shrine is glorified in the early medieval Tevaram poems.
story: Shiva, 'the lord who knows writing', is said to have submitted the temple accounts to the king himself to save a devoted accountant from punishment.
